lastCommit.message:
The iOS lane builds again on the API 36 stack

PROVEN REPAIR, merged only after the archive it was written for succeeded.

llama.rn 0.4.8's podspec pinned OTHER_CPLUSPLUSFLAGS to -std=c++17, which lands
last on the clang command line and overrides CLANG_CXX_LANGUAGE_STANDARD. React
Native 0.81 sets that standard to c++20 and its ReactCommon bridging header uses
a C++20 requires-clause, so RNLlama.mm could not parse it and every iOS archive
died at the same file. One flag, changed in the patch file that already patches
this package.

EVIDENCE — EAS build 94cd6c60-5322-48a3-8191-29e7ee41538b, from 3d43bb82:
  Xcode archive .......... PASSED (the gate every prior attempt failed)
  IPA export + upload .... PASSED
  auto-submit ............ PASSED
  TestFlight ............. Build 208 / 2.5.0 present and processing,
                           owner-confirmed on App Store Connect

This is the FIRST iOS binary produced on the migrated native stack — Expo 54,
React Native 0.81, React 19, new architecture — with llama.rn, onnxruntime and
ExecuTorch all compiling together.

THE THREE FALSE STARTS ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY. build-ios runs 204
and 206 were dispatched against this trunk before it carried the fix and failed
identically about twenty-five minutes in; EAS builds 205 and 207 are not evidence
about the repair. Only run 207, dispatched against the branch, ever compiled it.

ANDROID CANNOT REGRESS: a podspec is read only by CocoaPods, and the four Android
hunks in this patch file — the 16 KB page-size cmake argument among them — are
byte-identical. Play build 476 is untouched.

⚠ THIS PUBLISHES AN OTA TO GOLEM, AND IT IS EXPECTED. patches/ is deliberately
absent from ci.yml's publish-ignore list, because this same patch file carries a
src/index.ts hunk that IS bundled. The bundle is byte-identical to what golem
already runs and the stamp is unchanged at 2026-09-16-1825, so the dev phone will
receive an update that changes nothing it can see. That is cosmetic, it is the
known OTA-1482 shape, and it is the accepted cost of putting the repair on the
trunk. This merge title carries no line marker, so the publisher resolves golem
and the HAL audience is not touched.

No JS byte, no gameplay, no llama runtime setting, no versionCode, no OTA stamp,
no workflow, no credential.

pullRequest.title: llama.rn compiles at the standard React Native now speaks
pullRequest.message:
One line, iOS only. Unblocks the 2.5.0 TestFlight baseline. **Merge only after an EAS build proves it.**

## What failed

EAS build `14d5932e-18cf-428b-9f7b-43545d9fa1db` (2.5.0 / build 205, from `c94f9c5b`, build-ios run 204) reached Xcode and died at `** ARCHIVE FAILED **`, exit 65. Fourteen diagnostics, one defect:

```
ios/Pods/Headers/Public/ReactCommon/react/bridging/Base.h:65
  requires is_jsi_v<JSArgT>
  -> unknown type name 'requires'
```

`requires` is a C++20 requires-clause. The compiler didn't recognise it, so that translation unit was compiling as **C++17**. Every other error — `JSArgT` / `ReturnT` / `T` undeclared, `expected ';' after top level declarator` — is the cascade.

## Root cause

`llama-rn.podspec` forces the standard down:

```ruby
"OTHER_CPLUSPLUSFLAGS" => base_optimizer_flags + " -std=c++17"
```

An explicit `-std` on `OTHER_CPLUSPLUSFLAGS` lands last on the clang command line and **overrides** `CLANG_CXX_LANGUAGE_STANDARD`. RN 0.81 sets that to `c++20` (`helpers.rb:148`, applied by `new_architecture.rb:106`).

The differential is the proof — exactly one pod failed, and it's the only one forcing a standard:

| pod | C++ setting | result |
|---|---|---|
| `react-native-executorch` | sets `CLANG_CXX_LANGUAGE_STANDARD = c++20` (podspec:49) | clean |
| `onnxruntime-react-native` | no override, inherits C++20 | clean |
| `react-native-safe-area-context` | no override, inherits C++20 | clean |
| **`llama-rn`** | **forces `-std=c++17`** | **the only failure** |

ReactCodegen, the ONNX JSI bridge, ExecuTorch + `opencv-rne`, Hermes, Sentry and safe-area-context all compiled fine under RN 0.81. Pod install completed. Signing was never in question.

**Why it never bit before:** at RN 0.76.3 — build 199 and every prior iOS binary — `bridging/Base.h` used SFINAE, not concepts. RN moved that header to C++20. And llama.rn only pulls those headers when `RCT_NEW_ARCH_ENABLED=1`. The failure needs new arch **+** RN 0.81 **+** llama.rn 0.4.8 together.

**Not the cause:** the `Sentry-Sentry: iOS@11.0 deployment version mismatch` line is a pre-existing warning on Sentry's own pod, already documented as such in OTA-1824.

## The change

```diff
-    "OTHER_CPLUSPLUSFLAGS" => base_optimizer_flags + " -std=c++17"
+    "OTHER_CPLUSPLUSFLAGS" => base_optimizer_flags + " -std=c++20"
```

Carried in the existing `patches/llama.rn+0.4.8.patch`, applied by `patch-package` via `postinstall` on the EAS worker — the mechanism the Android 16 KB work established. Consistent with the standing rulings: GATE 7 classified *upgrading* llama.rn as **E**; GATE 7B classified *surgical patching of 0.4.8* as **A**.

## Evidence

- Patch regeneration is **purely additive**: `diff` before/after is a single +13-line block. All four Android hunks and the `src/index.ts` hunk are byte-preserved.
- Round-trip proven: clean `llama.rn@0.4.8` pulled from the registry, `git apply --check` reports all **six** files check clean; after apply the podspec reads `-std=c++20`, the Android 16 KB hunk and the src hunk are both present.
- One file changed. No `check:*` gate references `patches/`, pods or native.
- `OTA_BUILD_ID` deliberately **unchanged** at `2026-09-16-1825` — this ships no JS, so it earns no new stamp.

**Android cannot regress:** a podspec is read only by CocoaPods. Build 476 is already in Play from this same file's Android hunks, which are untouched.

**This cannot be compiled here** — Linux container, no Xcode, no CocoaPods. The validation is that the flag the compiler obeyed is now the flag RN requires, read out of both installed packages. Only the next EAS build can prove the archive succeeds, and nothing here claims it does.

## Why a branch and not the trunk

`patches/*` is **not** in `ci.yml`'s publish-ignore list (`ci.yml:439`) — correctly, since this patch file also carries a bundled `src/index.ts` hunk. Pushing this to `golem-line` would dispatch the publisher, and with no `[ota-hal]` marker it would republish a byte-identical bundle to the **golem** channel under the stamp the device already carries — the OTA-1482 confusion. Merge this once an EAS build is green.
